note: Newly delivered literature since the previous edition, including reviewed baseline/backfill records where exact first-online timing remains unavailable. Small is excluded by owner instruction. Research Square Nature Portfolio membership was verified through the visible filtered interface; all listed preprints remain unreviewed. Science publisher pages and editor credits could not be exhaustively verified, so the Marc Lavine inclusion rule remains only partially checked.

articles.title: Pressure-Gated Ionic Contact in Multilayered Nanomeshes Enables Strain-Insensitive Pressure Sensing
articles.summary: A 25-µm multilayer nanomesh forms ionic conduction paths only under normal pressure, while accommodating in-plane tensile deformation without a comparable capacitive response. Integrated on a soft jamming gripper, it maps object-dependent contact patterns during membrane deformation. The pressure-gated mechanism is a strong reference for suppressing strain artifacts in conformal tactile sensors.

articles.title: Distributed Haptic Chips With Materials’ Multifunctionalities for Dual‐Way Tactile Communication Enabled Terrain Recognition and Reconstruction in Robotic Teleoperation
articles.summary: Distributed haptic chips combine triboelectric, piezoresistive and piezoelectric sensing with pneumatic, thermal and high-frequency feedback. Multiple chips form a bidirectional tactile network that identifies terrain, body attitude and texture on a walking and climbing hexapod, then reproduces selected cues at the operator side. The architecture is directly relevant to distributed multimodal tactile arrays and closed-loop robotic interfaces.

articles.title: Fatigue‐Resistant Biaxially Stretchable Micro‐Origami Structured Electrodes
articles.summary: A prefabricated micro-origami pattern turns a Pt/Ecoflex bilayer into a regular biaxially stretchable electrode. The structure sustains more than 80% biaxial strain and 10,000 cycles at 50% strain while keeping sheet resistance below 20 Ω sq−1; a pressure sensor built from it classifies handwriting with 96% accuracy. The fabrication route is directly relevant to fatigue-resistant conductive traces and mechanically programmed sensor response.

articles.title: Programmable Auxetic Metamaterial‐Based E‐Skin for Conformable Dual‐Mechanism Spatiotemporal Sensing
articles.summary: A 4D-printed auxetic scaffold with a tunable negative Poisson ratio from −0.41 to −1.76 accommodates joint deformation and amplifies triboelectric and piezoelectric signals. A nine-channel array resolves 3 Hz running motion, while a one-dimensional convolutional network classifies movement states with more than 95% mean accuracy. The work provides a transferable strategy for mechanical amplification and crosstalk decoding in conformal sensor arrays.

articles.title: Ultrasensitive and Wide‐Range Ionic Pressure Sensors Toward Intelligent Assessment of Traditional Chinese Medicine Pulse and Oral Occlusal Health
articles.summary: An electric-double-layer ionic pressure sensor combines a reported peak sensitivity of 73,224 kPa−1 with a 0.01–1,100 kPa range. It records wrist pulses at three positions and classifies ten dental occlusal-pressure patterns in phantom tests. The wide dynamic range and multi-site pulse acquisition are relevant to pressure sensing, clinical palpation and decoupled physiological monitoring.

articles.title: Strain‐Insensitive Hydrogel Fiber Electrodes With Micropillar Arrays for Dynamic ECG Monitoring
articles.summary: Core–sheath hydrogel fibres and micropillar arrays form textile ECG electrodes with an 85% reduction in contact impedance and ~0.02% strain sensitivity. Garment-integrated recordings achieve a reported 21.56 dB signal-to-noise ratio during motion and support heart-rate-variability analysis over 24 h. The structural stabilization of the skin interface is relevant to long-term motion-tolerant physiological monitoring.

articles.title: Activation‐Free and Strain‐Resilient Island‐Bridge Liquid Metal Inks for Machine‐Learning‐Enabled Epidermal Electromyography
articles.summary: An activation-free liquid-metal ink uses Cu-decorated carbon-nanotube bridges between particles to maintain conductivity during deformation. Printed 100-µm features retain a sheet resistance of 0.13 Ω sq−1 at 300% strain, and a 12-channel breathable array records high-density surface EMG for exercise-state and fatigue analysis. The island–bridge network is relevant to fatigue-resistant wiring and motion-tolerant wearable arrays.

articles.title: Continuous and Wireless Monitoring of Myocardial Dynamics Using Biocompatible Magneto‐Viscoelastic Patches
articles.summary: A biocompatible epicardial patch containing ferromagnetic α″-Fe16N2 microparticles enables passive magnetic tracking of three-dimensional cardiac motion with an external magnetometer. Machine-learning regression reconstructs myocardial kinematics and detects acute diastolic dysfunction in rodents that was not apparent in surface ECG; the study also reports no adverse tissue response or systemic toxicity after 12 weeks. The combination of electronics-free transduction, vector magnetic readout and organ-motion reconstruction is directly transferable to magnetic implant localization and hemodynamic monitoring.

articles.title: Dynamically adaptive soft bioelectronics for neuro-immunomodulatory cancer therapy
articles.summary: A miniature subdiaphragmatic vagus-nerve stimulator combines an injectable anti-fatigue adhesive hydrogel, a deformable liquid-metal electrode and a battery-free wireless power module. In an orthotopic mouse model of pancreatic cancer, chronic stimulation suppresses tumour growth and metastasis and enhances anti-PD-1 response. The adaptive soft interface and compact wireless architecture are directly relevant to long-term implant stability and closed-loop bioelectronics.

articles.title: Metal-free magnets for bioresorbable biosensors
articles.summary: This research highlight discusses metal-free magnets for bioresorbable biosensors and places the underlying material advance in the context of transient magnetic implants. It is directly relevant to material selection for electronics-free sensing and to the trade-off between magnetic performance and resorption. Because the item is commentary, it does not constitute an independent experimental dataset and its author list was not available in the recovered metadata.

articles.title: A wireless magnetic implant system for continuous neuromuscular sensing
articles.summary: This study reports a wireless magnetic implant system for continuous neuromuscular sensing. The electronics-free magnetic transduction route is directly relevant to deep-tissue readout and motion-tolerant implant design. Quantitative performance details could not be recovered from the accessible metadata, so the summary is limited to the verified title and article identity.

articles.title: A strain-insensitive multiplexed soft microneedle patch for robust interstitial fluid biomarker monitoring
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
articles.summary: A soft microneedle array uses nano-hill topographies and strain-resilient electrodes to reduce motion-related signal variability by 14-fold. The 1.8 cm² system reports simultaneous glucose, tissue pH and temperature, with a glucose mean absolute relative difference of 10.8%. Its separation of a reusable electronic module from a disposable sensing array is relevant to robust multimodal monitoring during movement.

articles.title: A self-powered finger-worn wireless tracking interface for human-machine interaction
articles.summary: A 3.7 cm² finger-worn interface couples a triboelectric generator to a flexible electromagnetic transmitter, using fingertip motion itself to power wireless trajectory reporting. Three non-collinear receivers and machine-learning decoding provide sub-millimetre localization accuracy below 0.9 mm and reconstruct handwriting. The receiver geometry and inverse decoding strategy are relevant to compact magnetic localization and motion-tolerant human–machine interfaces.

articles.title: Gradient-interlayer–based flexible pressure sensors for high-performance robotic perception
articles.summary: A direct-ink-written gradient mesh controls progressive contact between an electrode and ionic hydrogel, separating bulk contact evolution from the local interfacial response. The device reports 175.9 kPa−1 sensitivity, a linear range to 360 kPa (R²=0.997), ~2.1 Pa detection limit and ~25 ms response, and extends to a three-axis force sensor. This is closely aligned with multiaxial tactile sensing, mechanical decoupling and scalable fabrication.

articles.title: Flexible guided-mode resonance cantilevers for non-contact optical sensing of sub-millinewton magnetic forces
articles.summary: Flexible guided-mode-resonance cantilevers are used for non-contact optical detection of sub-millinewton magnetic forces. The device links magnetic loading to a compliant resonant optical structure, making it relevant to magnetic–mechanical transduction and force calibration. Quantitative limits beyond the title-level claim were not recoverable from the accessible metadata.

articles.title: PEDOT:PSS-coated magnetoelastic sensors for highly sensitive wireless humidity sensing
articles.summary: PEDOT:PSS-coated magnetoelastic elements provide passive wireless humidity sensing through changes in their magnetic response. The design is directly relevant to biochemical or environmental signals converted into remotely readable magnetomechanical shifts. Detailed performance values were unavailable in the recovered metadata and are not inferred.

articles.title: A battery-free wireless implantable biosensor for postoperative breast cancer recurrence monitoring
articles.summary: This study reports a battery-free wireless implantable biosensor for monitoring postoperative breast-cancer recurrence. Its system-level combination of implantable biochemical sensing and passive telemetry is directly relevant to electronics-light long-term implants. Accessible metadata did not provide enough evidence to restate assay performance or in-vivo duration.

articles.title: Broadband Rheometry of Native Soft Tissues via i-Rheo-Indent
articles.summary: i-Rheo-Indent converts one force-relaxation and indentation history into a broadband viscoelastic spectrum without fitting a prescribed constitutive model. Tests on tissue analogues and mouse quadriceps, brain, colon and liver extend measurements to 500 rad s−1 and show that specimen preparation can materially change the inferred moduli. This preprint offers a transferable approach for measuring viscosity and modulus closer to the native tissue state and has not been peer reviewed.

articles.title: Low-Cost Real-Time Fiber-Optic Distance Sensing for OPM-based Biomagnetic Measurements
articles.summary: Nonmagnetic polymer-fibre sensors track the distance between optically pumped magnetometers and tissue over 0–30 mm at 2,048 Hz with a 16-ms response. Within 0–10 mm, pooled calibrations achieve adjusted R²>0.999 and a mean absolute reconstruction error of 0.0282 mm; wider-range calibration gives 0.1310 mm error over 10–30 mm. This is highly relevant to geometry tracking and motion-artifact correction in biomagnetic arrays; the preprint has not been peer reviewed.

articles.title: Scalable high-density tactile arenas for measuring ground-contact forces in freely moving animals
articles.summary: A modular tactile floor provides 16,384 sensing elements at 2-mm pitch across a 512×128 mm runway, using adaptive compressive sampling for nominal 1 kHz acquisition. Synchronized video resolves paw loading, stance, footprints, weight redistribution and centre-of-pressure trajectories; a longitudinal rat sciatic-injury model reveals load changes that gait timing underestimates. This preprint is directly relevant to distributed force sensing during free behavior and has not been peer reviewed.

articles.title: Tunable Magnetorheological Elastomer Substrates for Studying Mechano-Genetic Interactions in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
articles.summary: A dynamically tunable magnetorheological elastomer reproduces progressive mechanical stiffening for human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes. Stiffening selectively exposes pathological remodeling in MYBPC3-variant cells and promotes myofibroblast transition in primary cardiac fibroblasts. The magnetic control of substrate mechanics is directly relevant to magnetomechanical probing and disease mechanics; this preprint has not been peer reviewed.

articles.title: Self-Healing Magnetic Materials for Next-Generation Soft Electronics and Robotics
articles.summary: This review compares five self-healing mechanisms across magnetic gels, elastomers and other polymer networks. It examines trade-offs between magnetic performance, repairability, environmental durability and long-term use in sensing, robotics, energy systems and implantable devices. The framework is relevant to extending the service life of soft magnetic composites and interfaces.

articles.title: Fabrication Strategies and Performance Optimization Strategies of Flexible Brain–Computer Interface Electrodes
articles.summary: This review surveys flexible brain–computer-interface electrodes, including MEMS fabrication, printing and transfer, laser processing, thermal drawing, electrospinning, deposition and surface modification. It emphasizes mechanical matching, signal quality, spatial resolution, long-term stability and scalable manufacturing. These design and fabrication comparisons are transferable to soft implant arrays and chronic neural interfaces.

articles.title: Closed‐Loop Bioelectronics: From Functional Materials to Autonomous Therapy
articles.summary: This review organizes closed-loop bioelectronics from tissue-compatible materials through sensing, control and actuation to clinical systems. It identifies chronic interface stability, generalization of embedded machine learning, wireless power at tissue depth and regulation of adaptive combination products as central constraints. The synthesis is useful for positioning autonomous magnetic implants within the broader closed-loop therapy landscape.

articles.title: Where Ions Meet Electrons: Advanced Bioelectronic Interfaces With Organic Electrochemical Transistors
articles.summary: This review connects mixed ionic–electronic materials, electrolytes, OECT geometries and circuits through the design of biological interfaces. It covers electrophysiological and biochemical sensing, implants, wearables and emerging systems that combine sensing, memory, computation and actuation. The structure–property and interface discussion is useful for biochemical-to-electronic transduction and autonomous bioelectronic platforms.

articles.title: Comprehensive Acoustic Characterization of a Broadband Lateral MEMS Ultrasonic Transducer by Near-Field Acoustic Holography and Coupled Multiphysics Simulation
articles.summary: Near-field acoustic holography and coupled electrostatic–structural–thermoviscous simulation characterize a lateral CMUT from 10 to 60 kHz. The study attributes broadband operation to strong thermoviscous damping and validates radiation patterns, power and spherical-harmonic content against experiment. It is a useful engineering reference for MEMS resonance, damping and model validation; this preprint has not been peer reviewed.

articles.title: In-situ Control of the Photon-Magnon Synchronized Mode in a Miniaturized Magnetometer
articles.summary: A PCB-integrated photon–magnon magnetometer uses a variable resistor to tune coupling and the electromagnetic boundary condition in situ. A non-Hermitian model relates standing-wave interference to cusp-point formation and field responsivity. The compact tunable architecture is relevant to integrated low-noise magnetic readout; this preprint has not been peer reviewed.

articles.title: A synchronized dual-scale platform combining flexible micro-ECoG and skull-screw EEG reveals frequency-dependent cortex-to-skull spectral gain in awake mice
articles.summary: A synchronized platform combines flexible cortical micro-ECoG with skull-screw EEG in awake mice to quantify how cortical signals transform before extracranial recording. The dual-scale measurement is useful for separating source physiology from transmission and interface effects. It offers a validation framework for neural sensor arrays and signal reconstruction, although it is not a wireless implant study.

articles.title: Toward Wearable Joint Load Monitoring: Concurrent Estimation of Hip, Knee, and Ankle Sagittal Contact Forces from Sparse IMU Measurements
articles.summary: Four IMUs and a domain-informed multitask temporal network concurrently estimate hip, knee and ankle contact forces during daily activities. Leave-one-subject-out tests report average R² around 0.82 on the study dataset and 0.75 on an external dataset. The sparse-sensor reconstruction framework is relevant to distributed biomechanics and motion monitoring.

articles.title: Triphase MagRing-MPI: Topology Evolution and Vector Space Control for Electronic FFL Scanning
articles.summary: A three-phase, 200-mm-bore MagRing prototype electronically rotates and steers a field-free line using Clarke–Park control. It achieves a measured 0.071 T m−1 gradient, remains thermally stable for 35 min and localizes tracer targets over a 120×120 mm² head-phantom field; simulations indicate a possible 2.15 T m−1 gradient with soft magnetic cores. The work is a useful engineering reference for multichannel magnetic-field generation and calibration.

articles.title: A review of ring-type rotational MEMS traveling-wave ultrasonic micromotors: design, detection, control, and application validation
articles.summary: This review covers ring-type rotational MEMS traveling-wave ultrasonic micromotors from structural design and vibration detection to control and application validation. It is relevant to miniature actuation, resonance engineering and MEMS fabrication. As a review, it synthesizes existing evidence rather than reporting one new device benchmark.

articles.title: Optimal closed-loop feedback control of blood flow after spinal cord injury with norepinephrine
articles.summary: This work develops closed-loop norepinephrine control of blood flow after spinal cord injury. It is relevant as a control-system example in which continuous physiological sensing drives intervention under rapidly changing hemodynamics. Detailed quantitative outcomes were not present in the recovered metadata and are therefore not inferred.

articles.title: A stethoscope woven into fabric
articles.summary: This commentary highlights a fabric-integrated stethoscope for wearable cardiac monitoring. The textile form factor offers a useful comparison for conformal, long-duration acquisition of mechanical cardiovascular signals. It is an interpretive article rather than a new experimental study.

articles.title: A lightweight portable ultrasound robot for autonomous liver sonography
articles.summary: A lightweight portable robot performs autonomous liver ultrasound. The system is relevant to reproducible probe placement, mechanical contact control and automated clinical imaging outside conventional scanner workflows. Detailed accuracy and patient-cohort evidence were not available in the recovered metadata and are not inferred.

articles.title: Holographic focused ultrasound enables multitarget EV and MSC delivery for neurovascular repair after ischemic stroke
articles.summary: Holographic focused ultrasound is used for multitarget delivery of extracellular vesicles and mesenchymal stem cells after ischemic stroke. The work is relevant to non-invasive energy delivery and spatial targeting in deep tissue. The transferable value lies in beam control and neurovascular intervention rather than magnetic sensing.

articles.title: Cellular-resolution three-photon ultra-deep imaging (TrUDI) of neuronal population activity at 2-mm depth in the mammalian brain
articles.summary: The TrUDI three-photon system co-optimizes laser, optics and acquisition parameters to increase detected fluorescence yield by ~250-fold at the same laser power as earlier approaches. It records cellular-resolution neuronal activity at depths up to ~2 mm over ~230×230 µm² fields at 8.6 Hz in mouse cortex and hippocampus. Although optical rather than magnetic, the work is a useful benchmark for deep-tissue signal collection and safety-constrained system optimization.

articles.title: Wearable sensing of muscle dynamics towards anthropometric control
articles.summary: This article reports wearable sensing of muscle dynamics for anthropometric control. The topic aligns with continuous muscle-mechanics measurement and the translation of physiological motion into control signals. Quantitative evidence was not included in the accessible metadata and is not supplemented by inference.

articles.title: Asymmetric vibration pattern enables ultrafast locomotion of an insect-scale amphibious microrobot
articles.summary: This preprint reports an insect-scale amphibious microrobot whose asymmetric vibration pattern produces rapid locomotion across different environments. The mechanism is relevant to converting oscillatory drive into controlled motion in miniature robotic systems. Nature Portfolio screening was verified on the platform, but that status does not imply journal acceptance or peer review.

articles.title: Chemically Reconfigurable Neuromorphic Electronics for Neurochemical Homeostasis
articles.summary: This preprint describes chemically reconfigurable neuromorphic electronics designed to regulate neurochemical homeostasis. The concept links biochemical state sensing with adaptive electronic response and therefore offers a possible route toward closed-loop biochemical-to-electrical transduction. Experimental scope and performance are reported only as preprint evidence; Nature Portfolio screening does not imply acceptance.

articles.title: Programmable robotic textile with closed-loop self-sensing and active actuation
articles.summary: This robotic textile interlaces liquid-metal/liquid-crystal-elastomer fibres with passive yarns to integrate preload, strain and temperature sensing with low-voltage actuation. The shared core–sheath architecture supports closed-loop sensing, control and programmable morphing without a tether. It offers a materials and systems reference for wearable interfaces that combine sensing and actuation.

articles.title: Bioinspired soft enteroscopic robot for intestinal locomotion, steering, and intervention
articles.summary: A soft enteroscopic robot integrates intestinal locomotion, steering and therapeutic intervention. In pig experiments it traverses a collapsed, tortuous small intestine and supports biopsy and localized fluid delivery, demonstrating a clinically oriented combination of mobility and intervention. Its tissue-safe propulsion and navigation are relevant to sensing-enabled miniature robots, although sensing is not the central contribution.

articles.title: Distributed brain-spinal cord dynamics during micturition revealed by functional ultrasound imaging
articles.summary: Functional ultrasound maps region-specific hemodynamic activity in the brain and lumbosacral spinal cord during controlled bladder filling and voiding in rats. Population activity decodes bladder-pressure dynamics, linking distributed neural signals to a peripheral mechanical state. The work suggests a route toward neural interfaces for bladder control; this preprint has not been peer reviewed.

articles.title: A physics-informed peripheral hemodynamic digital twin for personalized estimation of arterial stiffness
articles.summary: A physics-informed digital twin estimates central–brachial arterial stiffness from one brachial pressure waveform rather than paired recording sites. In 118 participants, adding model-derived parameters improves blind-test pulse-wave-velocity estimation from r=0.22 and RMSE=1.90 m s−1 to r=0.67 and RMSE=1.12 m s−1. The PDE-constrained personalization is relevant to inverse reconstruction from sparse physiological sensors.

articles.title: A bio-inspired energy-resilient wireless skin
articles.summary: This article reports a bio-inspired energy-resilient wireless skin. The system concept is relevant to robust untethered sensing when power availability and deformation vary over time. The article was recovered as a previously unpushed baseline item; quantitative details were not available in the accessible metadata.

articles.title: Inverse origami inspired by insect morphogenesis: geometric design of wrinkle structures for curved surface formation
articles.summary: An inverse-origami framework derives a spatial wrinkle field from a target curved surface, then realizes the design through simulation and 3D-printed prototypes. The method encodes surface shape through programmed unfolding rather than conventional folding. This is an adjacent design tool for mechanically guided three-dimensional sensor structures; the preprint has not been peer reviewed.

articles.title: Directional endothelial intelligence enables hierarchical prioritization of local mechanical signals
articles.summary: This study examines how endothelial cells hierarchically prioritize directional local mechanical cues. The biological mechanism is adjacent to sensor engineering but relevant to interpreting the mechanical stimuli presented by blood flow. Quantitative results were not available in the recovered metadata and are not inferred.

articles.title: III-nitride-based in-sensor computing enabled by interfacial polarization effects
articles.summary: A III-nitride heterostructure uses interfacial polarization to separate photocarriers and switch between sensor–memristor and high-speed detector operation. The device reports nanowatt-per-square-centimetre sensitivity, responsivity near 10⁶ A W−1, on/off ratios near 10⁵ and operation up to 300 °C. Its relevance is methodological: local sensing and computation may reduce data-transfer load in dense arrays.

articles.title: Ultrasonic Detection of Venous Gas Emboli and Tissue Gas in Rodents: Toward Imaging Biomarkers for Decompression Stress
articles.summary: Serial cardiac and renal ultrasound in decompressed rats links venous-gas-embolus grade with modeled decompression risk and tissue-gas signatures. Renal grayscale intensity falls from 67.0 to 60.7 arbitrary units between low and higher embolus grades, with histology showing voids consistent with gas. This is an adjacent example of quantitative ultrasound biomarkers under changing flow conditions; the preprint has not been peer reviewed.
